{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "Use Welch's ANOVA if homogeneity of variance is violated; otherwise use standard one-way ANOVA",
    "For Success (binary: 0/1), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA, as linearity and normality assumptions are violated",
    "Include Mouse as a random effect in mixed-effects models to account for repeated measures across the 8 mice (n=76655 trials, 8 subjects)",
    "Report eta-squared or partial eta-squared as effect size for significant ANOVA results"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If main effect of Stim Paradigm is significant for continuous variables, perform pairwise comparisons using Tukey's HSD for standard ANOVA or Games-Howell for Welch's ANOVA",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use pairwise z-tests for proportions with multiple comparison correction",
    "Focus post-hoc comparisons on Combined vs Sham (primary contrast), ICMS Only vs Sham, and visual conditions vs ICMS Only to assess additive/synergistic effects",
    "Report 95% confidence intervals for all pairwise differences",
    "Flag comparisons where Combined differs from both unimodal conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) as evidence for multimodal integration effects"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at q=0.05 across all pairwise tests within each response variable; for family-wise error control across the 5 response variables, apply Bonferroni correction (adjusted alpha = 0.01) or use hierarchical testing where ANOVA must be significant before post-hoc tests are interpreted",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as the categorical response (5 levels) and the five performance variables as predictors. This is appropriate because: (1) Stim Paradigm is categorical with no natural ordering, (2) we want to predict which paradigm produced a given performance profile, and (3) multinomial logit directly models P(Stim Paradigm | performance) or equivalently the reverse with appropriate sampling assumptions. Alternative: Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) or quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA) if multivariate normality holds; random forest or gradient boosting if non-linear relationships are suspected. Given the large sample (n=76655), recommend starting with multinomial logistic regression with LASSO regularization for variable selection and interpretability, with Mouse as a random effect or stratification variable.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals for each Stim Paradigm group; consider log-transformation for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency given right-skew (max values >> mean + 3*sd)",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Levene's test; use Welch's ANOVA or robust standard errors if violated",
    "Independence: Check for autocorrelation in trial sequences within mice; use mixed models with AR(1) structure if temporal autocorrelation detected",
    "Multicollinearity: Examine correlations among predictors (Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD likely correlated) before predictive modeling; VIF < 5 rule",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined has 63.7% of trials (48846/76655) vs 4.3% for Bright Visual Only (3323/76655); use weighted procedures or resampling to check robustness",
    "Complete separation check for multinomial logistic regression: ensure no performance variable perfectly predicts any single paradigm"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined condition expected to show fastest Time-to-Target, highest Success rate, and highest Path Efficiency compared to unimodal and Sham conditions, consistent with multimodal integration benefits",
    "ICMS Only likely intermediate between Combined and Sham, with Dim Visual Only potentially showing more variable performance due to low luminance",
    "Bright Visual Only may approach or exceed ICMS Only performance depending on visual salience, but unlikely to match Combined",
    "AD (angular dispersion) expected to be lowest in Combined and highest in Sham, reflecting more direct trajectories with multimodal guidance",
    "Success rates: Combined > ICMS Only ≈ Bright Visual Only > Dim Visual Only > Sham, based on mean success of 0.73 overall with substantial paradigm-driven variation",
    "Average Speed may show ceiling effects or less paradigm sensitivity than directional metrics (Path Efficiency, AD)"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in Stim Paradigm frequencies (Combined: 63.7%, Bright Visual Only: 4.3%) reduces power for comparisons involving rare conditions and may bias parameter estimates in predictive models",
    "No information on trial sequence, learning effects, or session structure; potential confounding of stimulation paradigm with practice or fatigue if not counterbalanced",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme right skew (max=29.8 vs mean=0.47), suggesting outlier trials or calculation artifacts that may violate assumptions",
    "AD bounded at [0,1] with mean 0.38, sd 0.24, approaching boundaries; variance-stabilizing transformation (arcsine or logit) may be needed",
    "Single replication (Run 1) with temperature=0.5; no assessment of LLM output stability or sensitivity to prompt variations",
    "Mouse as blocking factor has unequal trials (10986 vs 7233), potentially unbalanced random effects",
    "No baseline performance metrics or pre-stimulation data to establish within-mouse change scores"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression model with Stim Paradigm as response, all five performance variables as fixed-effect predictors (with appropriate transformations: log Time-to-Target, logit AD, standardized Path Efficiency and Average Speed), and Mouse as random intercept; compare to random slope models using AIC/BIC; validate predictive accuracy with stratified 5-fold cross-validation preserving Mouse identity; then conduct permutation-based importance analysis to rank which performance variables best discriminate paradigms, with particular attention to whether Combined trials are correctly classified versus confused with ICMS Only or visual conditions."
}
